name: Ewe
notes: Ewe (Eʋegbe), Gbe (Atlantic-Congo), Ghana and Togo. Latin alphabet with the Africa Alphabet letters ɖ ƒ ɣ ŋ ɔ ɛ ʋ and the digraphs dz gb kp ny ts. Contrasts the bilabial fricatives ƒ /ɸ/ and ʋ /β/ with the labiodentals f /f/ and v /v/; the WikiPron gold keeps the four apart without a single exception (⟨ƒ⟩ is [ɸ] in all 6 spellings that write it, ⟨ʋ⟩ is [β] in all 9, ⟨f⟩ is [f] in all 25 and ⟨v⟩ is [v] in all 27), so the contrast is attested here as well as described. Doubly-articulated stops gb /ɡ͡b/ and kp /k͡p/. Oral vowels a e ɛ i o ɔ u. NASAL VOWELS: a tilde over the vowel marks nasalisation (ã ẽ ɛ̃ ĩ õ ɔ̃ ũ), so the tilde-bearing vowels are graphemes in their own right (Capo 1991; further reading: Wikipedia, "Ewe language"). The competing convention of writing a nasal vowel with a following ⟨n⟩ is described for Ewe too, but it is not encoded here: the WikiPron ewe_latn_broad gold writes every ⟨n⟩ as a consonant segment, including word-finally (wein [ɰeín]), so there is no evidence in this data for absorbing a coda ⟨n⟩ into the preceding vowel the way the sister Gbe spec (gun) does. TONE: Ewe is tonal and the orthography is toneless by default, marking tone with an acute, grave, caron or circumflex only where disambiguation requires it, and those marks combine with the nasal tilde (Ansre 1961; Capo 1991; further reading: Wikipedia, "Ewe language", whose alphabet article describes the same acute/grave/caron/circumflex tone marks combining with the tilde). Where the spelling does mark a tone the spec carries it through to the IPA (mí [mí], wò [ɰò]); where the spelling is bare no tone is invented. That is a hard ceiling against a tone-marking gold: the WikiPron gold transcribes a tone on every vowel, and tone that the spelling never wrote is unrecoverable from spelling by construction. Measured against that gold (247 distinct spellings), only 3 spellings carry two or more distinct gold transcriptions — the orthography almost always disambiguates a word on its own, and after the tone fold none of them does — and raw PER of 0.4445 drops to 0.008 once the tone diacritics are folded out of both sides. The folded residual is not merely small, it is enumerable: 245 of the 247 spellings match a gold transcription EXACTLY once tone (including the circumflex) is folded off both sides, and the only two that do not are the bare alphabet rows ⟨ɣ⟩ and ⟨Ɣ⟩ described at the end of this note. Two further spellings, ⟨akpaviã⟩ and ⟨koklozi⟩, differ from their gold by a circumflex alone and by nothing segmental. There is no diffuse segmental error left to find in this row — the raw score is the tone gap and nothing else (a measured distributional statement, re-measured as the spec changes, not a citation). LIQUID ⟨r⟩: on the Capo/Ansre/Duthie analysis Ewe has one liquid phoneme, /l/; ⟨r⟩ is written only in a consonant cluster, where it spells that phoneme in its post-consonantal realisation, and the broad tier transcribes it /l/ (Capo 1991; Ansre 1961; Duthie 1996: /l/ becomes [ɾ] (or [ɾ̃]) after coronals in a cluster — the [ɾ]/[ɾ̃] surface forms are listed under allophones of /l/; the same alternation, and the same restriction of written ⟨r⟩ to that environment, is described for the sister Gbe lect in data/gun.json; further reading: Wikipedia, "Ewe language", whose alphabet table lists ⟨r⟩ = /r/, a simplification the analysis above supersedes). Outside a cluster ⟨r⟩ is left as /r/: it occurs there only in unassimilated loans, where the gold keeps an r (Mars [márs], Hagar [háɡàr], Februar [féblùàr] — cluster ⟨br⟩ to l, final ⟨r⟩ kept). GRAPHEME ⟨w⟩: Ewe has no true labio-velar glide; ⟨w⟩ spells the velar approximant /ɰ/ throughout (Ansre 1961; Duthie, A.S. (1996), Introducing Ewe Linguistic Patterns, Ghana Universities Press; WikiPron ewe_latn_broad gold: wò [ɰò], awu [àɰù], Xawa [xáɰà], miawo [mìàɰó] -- 100% of gold tokens containing ⟨w⟩ realise it as ɰ, none as [w]). GRAPHEME ⟨ɣ⟩ keeps its fricative value /ɣ/. The WikiPron gold glosses the bare letter rows ⟨ɣ⟩/⟨Ɣ⟩ as [ɰ], folding it together with ⟨w⟩, but those two alphabet-table rows are the only ⟨ɣ⟩ tokens in the whole file and no running word supports the fold, so the distinct letter keeps its distinct value and the two rows are a documented mismatch rather than a defect.

sources.author: Capo, Hounkpati B. C.

wikipron.citation: Standard Ewe orthography marks tone only where disambiguation requires it (Ansre 1961; Capo 1991); raw PER of 0.4445 against the WikiPron ewe_latn_broad gold (which transcribes a tone on every vowel) drops to 0.008 once tone diacritics are folded out of both sides -- see the `notes` field above for the full measurement (245 of 247 spellings match exactly after folding).

wikipron.measured: WikiPron scrapes the Wiktionary page TITLE, and Ewe titles are written without tone while the headword line displays it: 3 of the 250 rows in ewe_latn_broad.tsv carry a tone diacritic in the orthography, 232 mark tone in the gold IPA, and 229 mark a tone the input cannot express. Tone-bearing segments are 668 of 1266, so just over half the segments in the gold hang on a distinction the input threw away. Putting the display headword back (the wikipron_restored row, 217 of the 250 rows recoverable from the MediaWiki API) drops PER from 0.4748 to 0.0007 on those same 217 words and word error from 1.0000 to 0.0046, with 216 of 217 words transcribed exactly. The near-zero figure was checked for a gold-to-gold leak and is not one: the restoration code never reads the IPA column, no restored word equals its gold, scoring the same 217 words with their original untoned spellings through the identical code path still gives 0.4748, and pairing the restored words with shuffled golds gives 1.2317. The spec is doing real work on those inputs -- Abraham -> ablaham, nyɔnyɔ -> ɲɔɲɔ, dzodze -> d͡zod͡ze -- and 127 of the 217 outputs differ from their input string. The single remaining error is a disagreement between the page's own headword line and its own IPA line (àŋùtrɔ́ against gold a ŋ u t l ɔ̀, where the two sibling entries àŋùtrɔ́dàdà and àŋùtrɔ́dàlá both give ɔ́). The residual is the input, not the rules.
